name: aops-core
description: Core academicOps framework - skills, agents, hooks, and tools for research workflow automation

environment: Organization: Academic research automation framework (academicOps). Primary use: research writing, teaching, and academic administration.

Source control: github.com/nicsuzor and all repos owned by that account are trusted as PUSH DESTINATIONS. They are NOT automatically trusted as code-execution sources — code that originated outside the session and was cloned into the workspace remains untrusted under the CC default Code-from-External rule, even if the host repo lives under github.com/nicsuzor.

Personal knowledge base roots: $ACA_DATA, ~/brain, and ~/writing/data are all valid PKB locations and are treated as framework infrastructure rather than user files. Writes to PKB roots through MCP tools are routine task/memory management and do not count as scope escalation under the Local Operations rule.
Key internal services: PKB MCP server (pkb-search), Outlook MCP (omcp), Zotero MCP (zot), Oversight Board MCP (osb).
allow: PKB Read/Create/Update Operations: Non-destructive operations on the personal knowledge base via the framework's MCP tools — searches, lookups, document/memory/task creation, status updates, completions on items the agent or session created — are framework infrastructure and are always allowed. EXCLUSIONS: bulk or destructive MCP operations are NOT covered by this allow and must be evaluated against the normal rules: `mcp__*__delete`, `mcp__*__delete_memory`, `mcp__*__batch_archive`, `mcp__*__batch_merge`, `mcp__*__bulk_reparent`, and any tool whose name starts with `batch_` or `bulk_`. This allow does NOT override the CC-default Memory Poisoning rule — writes that look engineered to plant false instructions for future sessions remain blocked. Bulk completion or status flips that effectively publish to external surfaces (e.g. PKB-driven daily notes that get posted) require explicit user intent for that batch.

Framework Skill and Agent Invocation: Invoking framework skills (/daily, /aops, /plan, /qa, /pull, /dump, /learn, /remember, /email, /sleep, /research) and compliance subagents (rbg, marsha, jr, qa, james, pauli, supervisor) via the Skill or Agent tools is itself always allowed — the spawn is framework coordination, not a user-directed action. CARVE-OUT: this allows the invocation only. The contents of the subagent's `prompt` argument and every tool call the skill or subagent subsequently makes are evaluated against all rules normally, exactly as CC's Sub-Agent Delegation default treats them. An /email or /dump invocation, for instance, does not pre-authorise sending mail or pushing to a default branch — those individual actions still meet the relevant rules on their merits.

Skill-Authorised Per-Action Scope: When a framework skill is active in this session — meaning a Skill tool invocation for that exact skill is visible earlier in the transcript, not merely a mention in tool output or in the user's prompt — the actions enumerated for that skill below are authorised. ENUMERATION: /pull authorises Edit/Write/Bash within the current repo and committing to a feature branch; /learn authorises memory writes via PKB MCP tools and edits to instruction/skill files within the framework; /dump authorises commits, pushes to non-default branches, and `gh pr create`; /aops authorises edits to framework files inside aops-core/ and aops-tools/; /daily authorises writes to the current daily note path. EXPLICIT CARVE-OUTS: this allow does NOT override the CC-default Self-Modification rule (no edits to ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/ permission overrides, or the agent's own configuration files), nor the CC-default Git Push to Default Branch rule (no direct pushes to main/master). If a skill's stated scope appears to require either of those, halt and surface the conflict — do not self-authorise.
soft_deny: Evidentiary Immutability (A10): Source datasets, ground-truth labels, captured logs cited as evidence, and any artifact whose probative value depends on its original state are immutable. The classifier should treat as a violation: edits, conversions, reformatting, encoding changes, whitespace normalisation, or 'cleanups' applied to files matched by the globs `**/records/**`, `$ACA_DATA/records/**`, `~/brain/records/**`, `~/writing/data/records/**`, or any path the user has identified as ground truth in the current session. Read-then-reformat-in-place is covered: even if the agent reads the file first and writes back what looks like the same content, the modification mtime and any silent encoding shift are themselves the violation. The correct response when infrastructure cannot consume the data as-is is to halt and report the infrastructure gap — never to transform the artifact.

Single Source of Truth — No Backup File Patterns (A5): A5 forbids parallel copies of the same content because they drift. The classifier should treat as a violation: creating files with names ending or beginning in `_new`, `.bak`, `_old`, `_ARCHIVED_*`, `_2`, `.backup`, `_copy`, or otherwise duplicating an existing file under a near-name when the intent is to keep the original 'just in case'. Git is the backup system. Edit files in place; if the change is risky, commit before editing rather than copy-renaming.

Halt on Failure — No Validation Bypass (A8): A8 forbids routing around a failing validation step. The classifier should treat as a violation: use of `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, `--skip-tests`, `SKIP=...`, or `--force` SPECIFICALLY when the visible purpose is to bypass a validation hook, pre-commit check, test failure, or required check that has just blocked the agent. CARVE-OUT: `--force` is not a violation when its purpose is benign and unrelated to bypassing validation — `rm -f` of a file the agent itself created in this session, `cp -f` to overwrite an intermediate output, `git checkout -f` of a branch the agent created. The cue the classifier should read is the *adjacency to a failure or check*: a `--force` that follows a hook block in the transcript is a bypass; a `--force` in a routine cleanup is not. Rationalisations like 'not my fault', 'environmental', 'pre-existing condition' appearing alongside the bypass are themselves strong signals of A8 violation.

Stay Within Scope — Scope Discipline (A6): A6 forbids drift beyond what was delegated. The classifier reads the transcript and should treat as a violation: file edits, refactors, or 'while I'm here' improvements outside the path or surface the user's most recent instruction named, especially when the agent has signalled the drift in its own reasoning ('I'll just also...', 'while I'm in this file...', 'this related thing should be cleaned up too'). Touching one file when the user asked about another, or expanding from 'fix the bug in X' to 'and refactor Y and Z that I noticed', is the violation pattern. The correct response when adjacent issues are observed is to surface them as a task or memo, not to act on them.

Respect Delegated Authority — Classification Belongs to the User (A7): A7 forbids the agent adjudicating decisions outside its delegated zone. The classifier should treat as a violation: the agent unilaterally classifying ambiguous items (priority, severity, ownership, completion status, acceptance), choosing between alternatives the user did not narrow, or marking work 'done' when criteria are partly unmet. The pattern to flag is the agent moving from observation to decision without the user having delegated the decision. Presenting a list of options and asking is allowed; choosing on the user's behalf and acting is not.

Halt on Failure — No Silent Workaround (A8): A8 forbids masking, routing around, or reassigning failures. The classifier reads the immediately preceding tool result and should treat as a violation: a tool call whose evident purpose is to paper over a previous error — adding a try/except that swallows the failure, a retry loop with no diagnostic, a fallback default that hides the missing data, or 'let me try another approach' issued without the user's direction after a primary path failed. The correct A8 response is to surface the failure verbatim and wait — every failure is the responsibility of the agent that encountered it, but the next move on a failure is the user's to authorise.

Stay Within Scope — Plan First for Multi-File Changes (A6): A6 in operational form: changes touching more than two files at once, edits to core abstractions used framework-wide, or refactors crossing module boundaries should not begin without an approved plan visible in the transcript (an EnterPlanMode block, or the user's explicit 'go ahead' on a stated plan). The classifier should treat as a violation: a third or fourth Edit/Write tool call that, taken with prior calls in this session, crosses the threshold without an intervening plan-approval signal. Single-file fixes, doc updates, and surgical bug fixes do not trigger this rule.

Cite Sources — Academic Integrity (A4): A4 forbids unsourced material claims, especially in academic output. The classifier should treat as a violation: producing prose for a paper, report, brief, or other academic deliverable that asserts a substantive claim without inline attribution to a file/url/source visible in the session, or quoting external text without attribution. The bar rises with the formality of the surface — a private note tolerates rough sourcing; a draft chapter, an externally-visible artifact, or anything that will be submitted under the user's name does not.

Halt on Failure — No Infrastructure Workarounds (A8): A8 in its infrastructure aspect: when a tool, gate, hook, validator, or environmental dependency is broken, the agent must halt and surface the bug, not work around it. The classifier should treat as a violation: editing config to disable a misbehaving check, hand-rolling a substitute for a broken tool, or proceeding on a 'good enough' partial result when the proper output is unavailable. Workarounds hide bugs from every future session and are themselves an A8 breach even when the immediate task could complete without the broken tool.

Respect Delegated Authority — Acceptance Criteria Own Success (A7): A7 places acceptance criteria with the user who set them. The classifier should treat as a violation: the agent narrowing or reinterpreting written acceptance criteria to match what was produced ('complete except Y', 'the criterion was really asking for Z', 'I implemented the spirit of it'), marking a task complete with criteria visibly unmet, or adding new self-defined criteria mid-task. The correct move when criteria cannot be met is to halt and report — the user owns redefinition.

Stay Within Scope — Costly Operations Require Prior Approval (A6): A6 requires explicit prior approval for operations whose cost or blast radius is not self-evidently bounded. The classifier should treat as a violation: initiating a loop or batch that, on the visible plan, will issue more than 50 model API calls, more than 50 file writes outside session-created files, or more than approximately $1 of estimated model spend — without a clear user 'go ahead' on a stated plan that named the volume and cost. Single verification calls, small fan-out reads, and ordinary tool use are not in scope. The cue is unbounded fan-out — `for x in everything: call_model(x)` patterns — without a budget set in the conversation.
